transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I hope it's okay that I'm here. I'm just... I guess I've been a little on edge lately? Well, honestly, I'm here because I keep... sort of blowing up at people over nothing. Which is really embarrassing to admit. 

Like, just the other day at the store, I yelled at one of my employees just because she put some stock on the wrong shelf. I felt terrible about it. Afterward, I was literally shaking. I promise you, that is absolutely not how I usually treat people. I try really hard to be a supportive manager, you know? I just feel so bad about it. Does that... does it make sense why I'd come in for that? I just don't want to be acting this way.
Have you had similar outbursts or feelings of intense irritability in situations outside of work, like at home or in traffic, for example?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But mostly it's just been that one big thing at work. I mean, like I said, I'm here because I just keep blowing up at people over nothing. It's so unlike me. 

Like with my employee and the shelves... I still can't believe I yelled at her like that. I was literally shaking afterward because it just felt so wrong. I know I already mentioned that, I just... I really want you to know that I'm usually a very patient person. I don't go around yelling at people in traffic or at home. It's just... lately, the smallest things seem to set me off, and then I feel awful about it. Is it okay that I'm focusing so much on the work thing? It's just the one that really scared me, you know?
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even when it's not entirely your fault?

Um... guilty? I mean... I do feel really guilty about yelling at my employee, obviously. I should have handled that better. But... I don't think I'm sitting around blaming myself for everything else in the world, if that's what you mean. 

I try really hard to take responsibility when I mess up, but I don't think I'm, like, beating myself up over things that aren't my fault. I just want to make sure I'm treating people right. Is that what you were asking? I hope I'm answering these questions okay. I just want to give you the right information so you can help me.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest or not getting pleasure from things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends, or other activities?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. I still enjoy reading and... and watching my shows and stuff. 

I don't think I've lost interest in anything. I try to keep up with my friends when I can, though work has been pretty busy. But when we do get together, it's still nice. I haven't really noticed any changes there. I mean, is it normal to lose interest in things when you're feeling on edge? I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Have you noticed yourself worrying a lot or feeling anxious about things more than usual, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I worry about normal things, I guess? Like making sure the store is running right or... or paying bills, just regular stuff. 

I don't think I'm sitting around feeling anxious for no reason. I try really hard to just keep moving forward and handle things as they come. I'm not a... I wouldn't call myself a worrywart or anything like that. I really hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right, because I know I've been so stressed lately, but I don't think I'm just anxious about everything all the time. Is that what you were looking for?
Have you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, even if just in the background, not necessarily intense enough to say you're depressed?

Um... no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling sad or down like that. I mean, I have my moments, just like anyone else, right? But I'm definitely not walking around feeling depressed all day. 

I try to stay positive and keep a smile on, especially at the store. You kind of have to in retail, you know? So, no, I don't think I've been feeling sad in the background or anything. I really hope that's helpful? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, falling apart completely. I'm trying my best to hold it together. Does that make sense?
Have you been having trouble sleeping, like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early, even if you feel tired?

Um... no, my sleep is... it's mostly fine, I think. I mean, I'm pretty tired by the end of the day, being on my feet at the store and everything, so I usually just kind of crash. 

I might wake up sometimes to adjust or whatever, but nothing out of the ordinary. I'm definitely not lying awake for hours or anything like that. I try really hard to keep a good schedule so I can be ready for work. I hope that's what you mean? I just want to be sure I'm doing okay with these questions. I'm really trying to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
Have you ever had episodes where you felt a sudden, intense surge of anger that made you act aggressively, even if the situation didn't really call for that kind of reaction?

Um... well... I guess I have had a few moments lately where I've been a little... easily frustrated? I don't want to say I'm an aggressive person, because I'm really not, I promise. But... I did have an incident recently that really scared me. 

I kind of... blew up at one of my employees. They just put some stock on the wrong shelf, which is a totally normal mistake, but I just lost it. I yelled at them, and... and afterward, I was actually shaking. It was just so out of character for me. I usually treat my team really well, and I felt so terrible about it afterward. I guess that's part of why I'm here, because I don't want to be that kind of boss. I really hope you don't think I'm a mean person? I'm just under so much stress, and I'm trying so hard to keep it together. Does that count as what you were asking about?

Have you noticed that you've been having ongoing difficulties with relationships or interactions with others, even when you're not feeling particularly stressed or upset, like often feeling misunderstood, holding grudges, or having trouble trusting people?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really hard to get along with everyone. I always want people to feel comfortable around me, you know? I definitely don't hold grudges or anything like that. I think I'm a pretty trusting person, maybe even too trusting sometimes. 

I mean, everyone has little misunderstandings now and then, right? But I always try to smooth things over quickly. I really value my relationships with my friends and my team at work. I don't want you to think I'm difficult to get along with, because I really do try my best to be a good friend and a good boss. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever had a pattern of unstable or intense relationships where you sometimes idealize someone and then suddenly feel angry or disappointed with them?

Oh... no, definitely not. I really try to be, um, very steady with people. I don't think I've ever been hot and cold like that with anyone. 

I mean, I really pride myself on being a loyal friend and a dependable person, you know? I don't just put people on a pedestal and then suddenly turn on them. That sounds... well, it sounds really exhausting, honestly, and I would never want to put anyone through that. If I care about someone, I stick by them. 

I really hope I'm answering these the right way for you? I just want to be sure I'm not coming across as, like, difficult or dramatic, because I really do try my hardest to keep things peaceful and stable with everyone in my life. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you been feeling empty inside or like something is missing in your life, even when things are going okay on the surface?

Um... empty? No, I don't think so. I mean, I have a good life, really. I have my job, and my friends, and I try to stay busy. I don't really sit around feeling like things are missing. 

I mean, everyone has days where they feel a little down, right? But I wouldn't say I feel empty. I try to be really grateful for what I have. I know some people have it a lot worse, so I always try to focus on the positive things. I really hope that makes sense? I'm trying to give you the best answers I can, I promise. I just don't think I've ever really felt that way.
Have you had episodes where your anger felt completely out of control, even if the situation didn’t seem to warrant such a strong reaction?

Um... well, this is really hard to talk about because I don't want you to think badly of me. I really do try to be a good boss, like I said. But... I guess I need to be honest with you, since it's actually kind of why I'm here. 

I've been... well, I keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. Like, just the other day at the store, one of my employees put some stock on the wrong shelf. It was just a simple mistake, right? But I just... I yelled at them. I got so upset, and right afterward, I was actually shaking. I felt so terrible because that is just not how I usually treat people at all. I always try to be so patient and encouraging with my team. 

I really hope you don't think I'm an awful person for doing that? I just... I don't know why I reacted that way, and it really scared me. I hope it's okay that I'm sharing this with you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's been going on.
Have you ever had a pattern of intense and unstable relationships where you sometimes feel extremely close to someone and then suddenly become very upset or distant from them?

Oh, um... I feel like maybe you asked me something kind of similar to this just a little bit ago? I hope it's okay that I mention that, I just want to make sure I'm following along right and not misunderstanding you! 

But no, my answer is still the same. I really don't have that kind of pattern. I try so hard to be very steady and reliable with the people I care about. I would absolutely hate to be the kind of person who is unpredictable or pushes people away like that. I really value my relationships, and I try to be a good, consistent friend and partner. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. Did you mean something a little different this time, or am I doing okay?
Have you had other episodes recently where you suddenly became extremely angry and lost control, even over small things, and felt really upset afterward?

Um, I think... wait, didn't we just talk about this? I mean, I hope I'm not being rude by pointing that out! I just want to make sure I'm not confusing you or messing up the interview. 

But, um, no, it's just been that one time at the store with my employee. I really haven't had any other times where I've lost my temper like that. I really try my best to be a calm and understanding person, and I would feel just awful if I was constantly blowing up at people over little things. That one time was bad enough, and I still feel so guilty about it. 

I really hope I'm answering this right? I just want to be as helpful as I can. Please let me know if you need me to explain anything else or if I'm not doing this the way you need me to!
Have you ever had similar episodes in the past where you suddenly became extremely angry and lost control, even over small things, and then felt really upset afterward?

Oh, um... no, never in the past. Honestly, I'm starting to worry just a little bit that maybe I've given you the wrong impression of myself? Since, um, we keep coming back to the anger thing... I promise I'm really not an angry person! 

Before that one time at the store, I have never, ever lost my temper like that. I've always prided myself on being really even-keeled and, you know, keeping the peace with everyone. I really hope you believe me? I just... I would hate for you to think I have this long history of flying off the handle, because I really, truly don't. That's why it scared me so much the other day. 

Am I answering everything okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and being helpful.
When you lost your temper at work, did you feel like hurting yourself or others, or did you actually push, hit, or throw something?

Oh! Oh, goodness, no. No, absolutely not. I would never, ever want to hurt anyone, and I definitely didn't want to hurt myself either. I really hope I didn't make it sound like I was violent or anything like that? 

I didn't push anyone, I didn't hit anyone, and I definitely didn't throw anything. I was just... I just raised my voice and got really upset, but I would never get physical. I try so hard to be gentle and kind, and the thought of actually hurting someone just makes my stomach turn. 

I'm really sorry if I gave you the impression that I was dangerous or out of control in that way. I promise it was just yelling. Does that make sense? I hope that's okay, I just really want to make sure you know I'm not a violent person! Am I explaining this right?
Have you noticed any significant problems in your personal life, family relationships, social interactions, or work performance because of these recent difficulties?

Um... well, I really try to keep everything running smoothly, I promise I do. But... I guess things have been slipping just a little bit lately? I'm so embarrassed to even admit this to you, because I've always been such a dedicated employee, but... I actually missed a vendor meeting the other day. And, um, there was one time I just had to walk out before my shift was finished. I felt so awful leaving my coworkers in a bind like that! 

And then at home... well, I just can't bring myself to face going back to the damaged house right now. So between that and work, my responsibilities are kind of... they're just piling up faster than I can handle at the moment. 

I'm really trying my hardest to get back on track, though! I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or irresponsible? I'm usually so on top of my schedule. I just feel terrible about letting people down. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this right now? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Can you tell me a bit more about the damaged house and how that has been affecting you emotionally?

Oh, the house... um... well, I know I really should be dealing with it like a responsible adult. I feel so silly even admitting this to you, because I know I need to handle it, but... I've just been completely avoiding going back there. 

And, um, it's actually not just the house itself. It's... even silly little things, like the mortgage folder, or... or even the herbs I had out on my patio. I just can't bring myself to look at them. Whenever I see anything tied to that day... my chest just gets so tight, and I just can't make myself go near it. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just running away from my problems? I want to be brave and face it, I really do, I just... I can't right now. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic or anything, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
Have you been having flashbacks, nightmares, or intrusive thoughts about the day your house was damaged?

Um... well... yes. I really hate to admit it, because I feel like I should be able to just... control my own thoughts, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around dwelling on it on purpose. But... the fire just keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere. 

I'll be trying to do something completely normal, like... I'll pick up a pan, or I'll just be opening a spreadsheet for work, and then suddenly... it's like I'm right back there. I can actually smell the smoke again, and I see the kitchen just filling up with it before I can even stop myself. 

I really try so hard to push it away and focus on the present, I promise I do, but it just sneaks up on me. I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or... or weak for not being able to block it out? Is it normal that my brain is doing that right now? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
